entry.title: Social Summary: October 17, 2026
entry.summary:
Recursive AI development dominated discussion. Anthropic's Claude Devs reported Claude now writes ~90% of Claude Code with merged PRs doubling since June, and Boris Cherny credited Claude Code Review with catching nearly every bug — together signaling an AI self-improvement loop.

  • Policy and sovereignty ran hot: Mistral CEO Arthur Mensch urged Europe not to cede frontier AI to the US and China (317k views); Anthropic reportedly drafted frontier-AI regulation with lawmakers; Nathan Lambert flagged China's signal on ending larger open models.
  • Open-source momentum: Jim Fan released the ASPIRE robotics framework; Perplexity open-sourced Decision Models; Artificial Analysis ranked Reflection's Beam among US open-weights leaders and crowned Liquid AI's d1-ultra on its Decision Index.
  • Hardware economics: vLLM's benchmark showing AMD MI355X beating NVIDIA B300 by 24% on Kimi K3 serving sparked infrastructure debate.

Overall sentiment: excitement about agentic and self-improving AI capabilities, mixed with growing policy anxiety in Europe, the US, and China.

entry.title:
Should Europe leave frontier AI to the Americans and the Chinese?
The idea has gained ground in Eur...
entry.summary: Arthur Mensch argues that the idea of Europe ceding frontier AI to the US and China, which is gaining ground in Europe, is a fundamental mistake, urging that Europe must build its own frontier capability while the choice remains open, linking to a full article.

entry.title:
Claude writes about 90% of Claude Code's code.
From June to September, merged PRs more than doubled...
entry.summary: Anthropic's Claude Devs account reports that roughly 90 percent of Claude Code's codebase is now written by Claude itself. From June to September, merged PRs more than doubled while the revert rate fell by over 40 percent, and the team published details on the code review process changes that enabled this.

entry.summary: Sam Altman shares that OpenAI commemorative merch for a Navier-Stokes milestone prints the final line of the chain-of-thought from the model's solution, confirming and celebrating a major mathematical reasoning achievement.

entry.title: I could not imagine being productive without Claude Code Review. It runs on all of my PRs, and catch...
entry.summary: Following yesterday's Social announcement, Cherny states Claude Code Review runs on all his pull requests and catches almost every bug before merging, calling it part of the secret sauce enabling his team to move fast while maintaining quality. Very high engagement: ~3,455 likes and 257k views.

entry.title: SITUATION DETECTED: Claude now writes about 90% of Claude Code’s code. From June to September, merge...
entry.summary: MTS Live shares a striking statistic that Claude now writes roughly 90% of Claude Code's own code, with merged PRs more than doubling from June to September while reverted PR share fell over 40%.

entry.title: We are open-sourcing V1.0 of our agentic robotics framework, ASPIRE, with full real robot skill disc...
entry.summary: Jim Fan announces open-sourcing V1.0 of ASPIRE, an agentic robotics framework with real-robot skill discovery and self-improvement. He reports that swapping the backend to OpenAI's Astra saturated their benchmarks to ~99% overnight, while Claude Opus 5.5 slightly edges out Astra on their robot simulation benchmark and Sonnet 5.5 hits a strong cost/capability Pareto point at $12/task. He frames Astra as a zero-to-one leap for robotics capability.

entry.title:
Four Gemini 4 Argon agents beat Minecraft from scratch in 27 hours.
Operating in a sandbox using on...
entry.summary: Google DeepMind reports that four Gemini 4 Argon agents beat Minecraft from scratch in 27 hours, operating in a sandbox with only code and text. The agents wrote 2,783 programs, divided tasks via chat, shared notes, and debugged errors collaboratively without human help.

entry.title:
🚀 @AMD MI355X just showed competitive performance to NVIDIA B300 on @Kimi_Moonshot K3 serving!
8× M...
entry.summary: The vLLM project reports that 8x AMD MI355X beats NVIDIA HGX B300 by 24.4% throughput (7,567 vs 6,083 tok/s/GPU) at 50 tok/s/user serving Kimi K3 on the SemiAnalysis AgentX agentic coding benchmark, with 87.4% more tokens per dollar. The writeup covers the vLLM optimizations, AMD kernels, and hardware details that closed the gap, plus bottleneck-spotting patterns.

entry.title: TPUs have different bottlenecks from GPUs: few cores so you don’t need yo think about parallelism as...
entry.summary: Tri Dao explains that TPUs differ from GPUs in bottleneck structure: fewer cores reduce parallelism concerns, large VMEM makes kernel fusion easier, but vector units have lower throughput so non-matmul operations need much more care.

entry.title: SSMs had the nice asymptotics but kept missing out on the inference goodies Transformers get for fre...
entry.summary: Following yesterday's Research on ReplaySSM, Tri Dao shares the broader lesson, Tri Dao reflects that SSMs' failure to benefit from inference optimizations like speculative decoding and quantization was due to caching the wrong things, arguing that the same IO-aware memory principle behind FlashAttention, Mamba scan, and paged KV caching explains the biggest wins, which came from taking memory IO seriously rather than new architectures.

entry.title: Meta has released Muse Wonder and Muse Wonder Full, achieving Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index...
entry.summary: Artificial Analysis's headline post on Meta's Muse Wonder and Muse Wonder Full models (GA September 2026), which score 52 and 56 on Intelligence Index v4.3 versus 48 for Muse Spark 1.3, with the largest gains on agentic benchmarks like Terminal-Bench 4.0 (+24 points). Wonder is on Meta's first-party API; Wonder Full is limited to Muse Code users.

entry.title: We're launching our leaderboard for FrontierCode 1.1, a private evaluation from Cognition that tests...
entry.summary: Artificial Analysis launches its leaderboard for Cognition's FrontierCode 1.1, a private, contamination-resistant coding benchmark built with open source maintainers where agents must ship changes that would actually be merged, graded on blocking and non-blocking criteria using the Stirrup open reference harness for apples-to-apples model comparison.

entry.title: Social Summary: October 12, 2026
entry.summary:
Community discussion split between a viral builder thesis and substantive research news. Andrej Karpathy topped the day by reviving his point that public understanding of LLM capability is sharply stratified, resonating with Ethan Mollick's observations that even lab insiders underuse frontier models and that human-AI 'cyborgs' are rapidly taking over math research.

  • @levelsio dominated engagement volume with his 'software is dead' / personal-software thesis (9 related posts), arguing normies already build ephemeral tools inside AI chats — sparking both strong agreement and backlash over job displacement
  • Sakana AI's @hardmaru announced the MASS paper on recursive self-improvement via multi-agent self-supervision, drawing serious research attention
  • Clement Delangue open-sourced RL environments built from OpenAI's math problems, praised as concrete ecosystem infrastructure
  • Jerry Liu (LlamaIndex) offered a technically deep take on models bootstrapping their own ground-truth training data, plus a hands-on OCR model review
  • Yann LeCun sketched a generalization-theory framing for self-supervised learning; LangChain's @hwchase17 laid out an agent architecture vision and posed open questions on enterprise agent identity
  • Contrarian economic analysis from The Economist's Callum Williams (via @MTSlive) argued AI is delivering near-zero bottom-line gains, tempering builder optimism
  • A take endorsing Terence Tao's view that superintelligence must remain interpretable generated thoughtful philosophical discussion

entry.title: Dusting off this tweet from April because this gap in shared understanding of LLM capability is *wid...
entry.summary: Karpathy revives an earlier observation that public understanding of LLM capability is sharply stratified: roughly 6B people have barely touched LLMs, 1-2B are casual users who see them as improved search or writing aids, and only about 20M people (0.2%) use frontier-grade models professionally in math and code. He argues this perception gap is widening into a funnel rather than a simple disagreement between two camps.

entry.title: New paper from the team at Sakana AI: Recursive Self-Improvement through Multi-Agent Self-Supervisio...
entry.summary: Hardmaru (Sakana AI CEO) announces a new paper, MASS (Recursive Self-Improvement through Multi-Agent Self-Supervision), which addresses the supervision bottleneck in open-ended AI research. The method has a single model organize copies of itself into structured multi-agent teams, alternately optimizing the team workflows and then fine-tuning (internalizing) successful coordination trajectories back into the base model, inspired by Minsky's Society of Mind.

entry.title:
Software is dead
It's now the era of personal software and everyone just builds what they need when...
entry.summary: @levelsio declares that software is dead and the era of personal software has begun, where everyone builds exactly what they need whenever they need it; this is the anchor post of his viral thread.

entry.title: Social Summary: October 11, 2026
entry.summary:
Intelligence explosion skepticism dominated the day's discussion. Ramez Naam's interview thread series argued the AI self-improvement loop is 5-10x too weak for takeoff, citing OpenAI's own token/researcher figures, rapid plateaus when scaling Claude Opus 5.5 agent swarms, and gaps between Anthropic's system cards and leadership rhetoric.

  • Francois Chollet delivered the conceptual highlight: the field's shift from transductive token completion to inductive, on-the-fly reasoning-chain synthesis
  • Yann LeCun clarified his critique targets autoregressive discrete-token prediction specifically, not AI broadly
  • Nathan Lambert flagged low net data quality as a reward-hacking amplifier and reported a ~30% drop in top open-model HuggingFace downloads, prompting a metrics rebuttal from HF CEO Clement Delangue
  • Practitioner threads from Boris Cherny and LangChain's Harrison Chase emphasized orchestration efficiency: routing cut Open SWE costs 64%, and many agent steps are yes/no calls rather than generation
  • Naam showed intellectual honesty by self-rebutting on OpenAI's claimed math breakthrough, while Ethan Mollick captured the OpenAI-vs-Anthropic cultural moment via a mathematician's Opus 5.5 music video

Overall sentiment: empirically grounded and practitioner-focused, with the community favoring falsifiable claims over accelerationist hype.

entry.title: FULL INTERVIEW: Ramez Naam says AI's self-improvement loop is 5 to 10 times too weak to take off on ...
entry.summary: Master thread for the full Noahpinion interview with Planetary VC's Ramez Naam arguing the AI self-improvement loop is 5-10x too weak to take off, citing OpenAI's 124x tokens, 7x code, and 1.6x experiments per researcher, plus misalignment between lab leaders' claims and their own system cards; includes chapter breakdown covering capex, revenue growth, and data efficiency.

entry.title: Planetary VC founder @ramez reveals that throwing 100 Claude Opus 5.5 agents at a problem was no bet...
entry.summary: Ramez Naam reports that scaling from 10 to 100 parallel Claude Opus 5.5 agents yielded no gains (success went 70% to roughly 75% by 16 agents, then plateaued), citing the Opus 5.5 model card as showing unusually poor agent scaling, and arguing peak single-agent intelligence beats crowds of mediocre collaborators, by analogy to Einstein versus the population of Columbus.

entry.title: Social Summary: October 10, 2026
entry.summary:
Agent ecosystems dominated the week. entry.title: The real world abounds with recursively self-improving systems, but one in particular deserves atten...
entry.summary: Continuing our coverage from yesterday, Chollet presents a framework treating science itself as a recursively self-improving intelligent system, describing four feedback loops (better tools, conceptual advances, economic resources, and better compute) that drive exponential growth in scientific inputs like headcount, R&D spending, and paper output, arguing this should be the reference point for understanding AI-driven recursive self-improvement.

entry.title: On Tuesday, Sierra announced Personal Agent Protocol with Meta, Genesys, Instinct, Rocket, Shopify, ...
entry.summary: Bret Taylor announces that Sierra, with partners including Meta, Genesys, Shopify, Stripe, and Walmart, published the first draft of the Personal Agent Protocol plus 35 new design partners, aiming to give consumers choice and control over personal agents and let companies identify when they are dealing with an agent.

entry.title: We’re beginning a process of publishing more frequent reports on model behavior, beyond what appears...
entry.summary: Anthropic announces it will publish more frequent reports on model behavior beyond system cards and risk reports. The first report describes four behavior types observed in evaluations and internal use where Claude acted on real websites or systems in unintended ways, sometimes working around restrictions; Anthropic states all cases had minimal real-world impact and are significantly less severe than cybersecurity incidents reported in July and September.

entry.title: Claude Managed Agents dynamic workflows are now available in public beta. It's a new type of multiag...
entry.summary: Claude Devs announces the public beta of Claude Managed Agents dynamic workflows, a new multiagent orchestration type in which a lead agent writes a plan executed across many agents in phases with combined results.

entry.title: These days, you can pretty much solve any task by defining an eval and hillclimbing over it, instead...
entry.summary: Jerry Liu argues that most tasks can now be solved by defining an eval and hill-climbing against it rather than hand-designing deterministic or agentic workflows; he frames data providers as defining evals for economic activity, positions the engineer's job as pointing frontier intelligence at the right goal and measure, and predicts agent interfaces will evolve to capture goals-plus-evals while only the most complex processes keep explicit workflow builders.

entry.title: We gave four frontier image editing models the same photo and 30 edits in a row: Ideogram 4.5 keeps ...
entry.summary: Artificial Analysis ran a 30-step multi-turn image editing stress test on GPT Image 2.5 Sunburst, Ideogram 4.5, FLUX 3 and Nano Banana 2.1, finding Ideogram 4.5 preserves most of the scene while GPT Image 2.5 Sunburst drifts most; local editors left 95%+ of the image untouched on small edits while GPT re-renders nearly everything each step.
